source.authors: Dutta S, Boruah B, Das A
source.title: New record of two natricine snakes, Hebius gilhodesi (Wall, 1925) and Herpetoreas davidi Nguyen et al., 2024 (Reptilia: Squamata: Colubridae), from India

eye: pupil as described for the new Indian material; side not stated
method: qualitative description of preserved museum specimens in the Description of new Indian material; Materials and methods (pieces joined): 'Morphological measurements and terminologies followed Das et al. (2021) as mentioned in the following: snout-vent length (SVL); [...] eye diameter (ED): horizontal diameter; eye to nostril distance (EN): anterior corner of eye to posterior edge of nostril; [...] interorbital distance (IO): measured at the anterior corner of orbit.' No pupil method is printed.
conditions: Not a type description: five Indian specimens of Hebius gilhodesi, described together in one paragraph (one species, one pupil value, no per-specimen pupil). Materials examined as returned by the page reader: WII-ADR1793 (adult male), WII-ADR1792 (adult female) and WII-ADR1800 (subadult female), Gandhigram, Changlang District, Arunachal Pradesh, India, 17-19 September 2022; WII-ADR3320 (adult male), Kamlang Tiger Reserve, Lohit District, 19 July 2023; WII-ADR3303 (juvenile female), Kamala Valley, Namdapha Tiger Reserve, Changlang District, 2 June 2023. The paper does not say whether the pupil was read on live or preserved animals or the constriction state. Anatomy only; vision not tested.
where: Results > Morphology > Hebius gilhodesi (Wall, 1925) > Description of new Indian material (Image 1); no Class, Order or Family heading is printed (the title prints '(Reptilia: Squamata: Colubridae)'); the fourth sentence of the description, beginning 'In lateral view tip of snout acute' (after the sentence ending 'last supralabial length.')
quote: In lateral view tip of snout acute; rostral partially visible; […] eye large with rounded pupil; orbit semi-circular, orbital diameter less than snout length; […]
note: new trait for the species: pupil_shape (same key as main). Not a repeat: grep of docs/ on main for Hebius gilhodesi and 10.11609/jott.10309.18.3.28479-28494 finds only eye_diameter_mm rows (desk-d490, from this paper), a family-placement remark in the notes of the desk-d497 Hebius citrinoventer rows, and progress or queue lines; no pupil_shape row. Quote opens at the start of the lateral-view sentence (the description's first sentence 'A moderate sized snake, SVL 370–410 mm in males and 250–370 mm in females.' is followed by the 'Body subcylindrical' sentence ending 'in females.' and the 'Head moderately distinct from neck' sentence ending 'last supralabial length.', so the pupil clause sits in the fourth sentence) and has two marked cuts; the cut middle holds loreal and preocular clauses with specimen exceptions (WII-ADR1792, WII-ADR1793), none about the pupil, and the cut tail holds postocular, temporal, labial and genial clauses (supralabials 'connected to eye' vary by specimen); no clause qualifies the pupil. A separate 'Colouration in life' sentence says 'pupil entirely dark with light outer margin' (colour, not filed). Reptile Database species page (reptile-database.reptarium.cz/Hebius/gilhodesi, reached from my own search 'Hebius gilhodesi new species Reptile Database') prints Hebius gilhodesi (WALL, 1925) with the comment that Bohra et al. 2025 revalidated gilhodesi (Wall himself synonymized it with khasiensis), and that the genetic and morphological differences may suit gilhodesi better as a subspecies of khasiensis; the synonymy lists 'Hebius gilhodesi — DUTTA et al. 2026'. Licence block as printed on the copy read (two sentences): 'Copyright: © Dutta et al. 2026. Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.', followed by 'JoTT allows unrestricted use, reproduction, and distribution of this article in any medium by providing adequate credit to the author(s) and the source of publication.' (read by audit 1330 from the JoTT HTML full text, opened from its own search results). Search that reached the paper: Hebius gilhodesi new species Reptile Database.

source.authors: Xu Y-H, Wang S, Ma S, Burbrink FT, Peng L-F, Huang S
source.title: First report of albinism for Achalinus sheni (Serpentes, Xenodermidae), with extended diagnosis of the species

eye: pupil as described for three newly collected females; side not stated
method: qualitative description of preserved females in the Expanded description of the females; Materials and methods (page-reader pieces joined; the reader's expansion '(eye diameter)' after ED is tooltip markup and left out): 'Specimens were humanely euthanized using lethal injection with 0.7% tricaine methanesulfonate (MS222) solution [...] Then the specimens were directly preserved in 75% ethanol'; eye-size passage: 'eye diameter (ED): taken from the most anterior corner of the eye to the most posterior corner'; 'All other measurements were performed using Deli digital calipers (DL312200) to the nearest 0.1 mm' (unit mm); no pupil method is printed
conditions: Three females described together: 'Based on three newly collected female specimens (field number: LFR2023008, LFR2023010, LFR2024015), an expanded description of the females is provided as below.' Specimens examined as printed (pieces joined): 'Three typical specimens: LFR2023008 (adult female), LFR2023009 (adult male), LFR2023010 (adult female); and one albinistic specimen: LFR2024015 (adult female), collected in July, 2023 from Yangshi Town, Lianyuan City, Loudi City, Hunan Province [...]; coll. by Shu Li and Ziyuan Feng.' Type material: none of these specimens is a type; this paper names no holotype, and 'paratype' appears only in the Figure 6 caption for ANU20230013 and ANU20230012 (adult males of the original series). Pooled within one species: the pupil shape is stated once for three females, one of them (LFR2024015) albinistic, and the paper does not give it per specimen; for the albinistic specimen it adds only 'The iris was blood-red, with a reddish pupil.' (colour, not filed). Wild-collected animals euthanized for preservation. Anatomy only; vision not tested.
where: Results > Taxonomic account > Reptilia > Serpentes > Xenodermidae > Achalinus > Achalinus sheni Ma, Xu, Qi, Wang, Tang, Huang & Jiang, 2023 > Expanded description of the females > Measurements and scalation (bold run-in label; the sentence begins 'Tail relatively short' right after it).
